transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Well, what finally scared me into making this appointment is that... I’ve been having these thoughts lately. Just thinking things like, if I didn’t wake up tomorrow, that might just be easier. I really want to be clear that I don’t want to actually hurt myself, but... just having those kinds of thoughts pop into my head really unsettled me. So, I figured it was time to come in and talk to someone.
How long have you been feeling this way—can you tell me when these low moods and thoughts first started?

Well, this low, flat feeling has been going on for about six months now. It's been present long enough that my usual routines just... aren't helping anymore. Things like my art classes or taking my morning walks—they just stopped feeling restorative. So, yeah, I'd say it's been about six months since it really set in.
Have you ever had a period, lasting several days or more, when you felt unusually energetic, elated, or irritable—very different from your normal self—even if it wasn't followed by a low mood?

Well, yes, actually. Um... right before this whole slump hit, I had a stretch like that. I felt, I don't know, almost too sure of myself. Like I had everything perfectly under control at work. But then... I would just snap at people over the tiniest things. Like, if my district manager questioned how I set up the floor layouts, I would get so irritated, which really isn't like me. So, yes, there was a period like that.
You mentioned feeling unusually confident and irritable before this low period started—about how many days in a row did that heightened state last?

I'm really not sure exactly how many days it was. I didn't think to keep track of it at the time. It was just... a noticeable stretch. Maybe a few days, maybe a little longer? I just know it lasted long enough to cause some tension at the store, but I couldn't give you a precise number.
During that stretch of feeling unusually confident and irritable, did other people—like coworkers or family—notice a clear change in your behavior?

Well, I don't know for sure if anyone else noticed a big change. I mean, my coworkers obviously noticed when I snapped at them, but... I don't know if they saw it as a whole shift in my personality or just me having a bad week. Nobody actually sat me down and said, "Hey, you're acting really different." So I'm not really sure how it looked from the outside.
During that stretch when you felt unusually confident and irritable, did you notice you needed less sleep than usual but still felt rested?

No, not really. Um... I think my sleep was pretty much the same as always. I didn't have any nights where I barely slept and felt perfectly fine the next day at the store. As far as I can remember, I was just sticking to my normal routine when it came to sleeping.

During that stretch when you felt unusually confident and irritable, did you notice yourself taking on more projects, spending more money, or engaging in activities that were riskier or more impulsive than usual?

I wouldn't say I did anything risky or spent a lot of money, but I definitely took on more projects at work. I was emailing my coworkers after hours, which really isn't like me. I kept proposing these new cultural promotion displays for the store, and I even offered to mentor some of the extra staff. It was just... I was filling up notebook pages with all these plans, honestly faster than I could actually carry them out.
Thinking back on that period of feeling unusually confident and irritable, can you tell me if it lasted at least four days in a row, even if you can't recall the exact number beyond that?

I'm honestly not sure if it was four days in a row. Um... it's a bit hard to remember the exact timeline now. It might have just been a couple of days, or maybe it was more broken up. I just didn't really keep track of the days like that while it was happening, so I can't say for certain if it lasted that long straight through.
Aside from this current six-month period, have you ever had a similar stretch of low mood, low energy, or loss of interest in things at any earlier point in your life?

No, I don't believe so. Um... before this recent stretch, I mean. This past six months is really the first time I've felt this low and just... drained of energy. I can't think of any earlier point in my life where I lost interest in things quite like this.

Can you think back to that time and tell me if the heightened, irritable feeling was still there when you went to work on, say, three or four consecutive shifts, or did it come and go within just a day or two?

I honestly couldn't tell you. Um... like I mentioned a minute ago, I just wasn't tracking the days. I remember being at work and feeling that way, but whether it stayed with me for three or four shifts in a row, or if it just came and went over a day or two... I really don't know. It's just hard to separate the days looking back on it now.
During that period of feeling unusually confident and irritable, did you notice your thoughts racing or that you were talking much faster than usual?

No, I didn't really notice anything like that. My thoughts seemed normal to me, just... maybe focused on whatever I was doing. And nobody mentioned that I was talking faster or anything. So, no, I don't think so.
Can you recall whether that heightened, irritable period continued through an entire weekend or spanned from one work week into the next, so we can pin down if it lasted at least four days in a row?

Like I said before, I just don't remember the timeline. I know I was feeling that way, but I couldn't tell you if it went through a whole weekend or bled into the next week. I just wasn't keeping track of the days like that, so I really can't say if it was four days in a row.

During that period when you felt unusually confident and irritable, did it cause any real problems—like conflicts with your manager or coworkers, or issues in your personal life—that were different from your normal day-to-day stress?

No, not really. I mean, I might have been a bit more on edge, but it didn't cause any big blowups at work or anything like that. I was still doing my job as a supervisor just fine, and nobody pulled me aside to complain about my attitude. And at home, things were pretty much the same as always. So, no, I wouldn't say it caused any real problems.
During that period when you felt unusually confident and irritable, did anyone close to you outside of work—like a friend or family member—comment that you seemed different or 'not yourself'?

No, nobody said anything like that. My husband didn't mention anything, and my friends didn't either. I think I just seemed like my usual self to them, maybe just a little more focused or something. But no one actually came out and said I was acting different.
Even without exact day counts, would you say that confident, irritable stretch felt more like it lasted less than a week, or did it seem to stretch on for a week or more?

I honestly just don't know. It's hard to look back and gauge the time like that. It might have been less than a week, or it could have stretched longer... I just didn't log it in my memory. I know that's probably not very helpful, but I really can't say one way or the other.
